candidates.name: Museo dell'Opera del Duomo
candidates.alt: Museum of the Works of the Duomo
candidates.content: This houses original artworks from the Duomo and surrounding religious buildings, including sculptures by Donatello, a Michelangelo Pietà (different from his version in Saint Peter's, Rome) and the losing entries in the 1401 conte

candidates.name: Galleria degli Uffizi
candidates.price: High season (21 Feb-9 Nov; 21 Dec-9 Jan): adult €29 (or €23 for early morning tickets: 08:15 and 08:30), conc €6, combi with Pitti & Boboli €38; low season: adult €16, conc €6, combi €18; including a booking fee of €4
candidates.hours: Tue-Sun 08:15-18:50, Mon closed, last admission 18:00; you may not bring in water
candidates.content: Outstanding fine art museum with Renaissance paintings and sculptures from classical antiquity. It's in a late 16th-century palazzo designed by Vasari, in two wings enclosing a long narrow courtyard, effectively a street, an innov

candidates.name: Bargello
candidates.hours: Daily Apr-Oct: 08:15-17:00, Nov-Feb: 08:15-14:00, but closed 2nd & 4th Sun and 1st, 3rd & 5th Mon of each month
candidates.content: Used as a barracks and prison until the 19th century, this museum houses some of the best Renaissance and Mannerist sculpture. Big names here include Michelangelo, Donatello, Ammannati, Bandinelli, Andrea and Jacopo Sansovino, Des

candidates.name: Galleria dell'Accademia
candidates.content: Highlights are Michelangelo's original David (the one in Piazza della Signoria is a copy) and his unfinished Slaves. It also includes Florentine painting, a museum of musical instruments, and Russian icons. No photography is allow

candidates.name: Palazzo Pitti
candidates.price: Mar-Oct: adult €16, conc €8, combi with Uffizi & Boboli €38; Nov-Feb: adult €10, conc €5, combi €18; booking fee €4
candidates.content: The original Pitti was a banker; the palace has housed royalty but became best known for its Medici family treasures. It's now divided into four museums (same ticket): ground floor is the Treasury of the Grand Dukes; first floor h

candidates.name: Museo Galileo
candidates.content: This museum shows the evolution of the instruments used in various scientific fields such as mathematics, physics, biology, chemistry, astronomy. The room of Galileo Galilei shows some of his original instruments as well as models

candidates.name: Palazzo Vecchio
candidates.price: "Museum" or "Tower and Battlements": €12.50 adults, €10 concessions. "Museum" and "Tower and Battlements": €17.50 adults, €15 concessions
candidates.content: Old city palace/city hall, adorned with fine art. The replica of Michelangelo's "David" is placed outside the main door in the original location of the statue, which is a symbol of the Comune of Florence. The site displays an impo

candidates.name: Ponte Vecchio
candidates.content: The oldest and most celebrated bridge over the Arno, and the only Florentine bridge to survive World War II. The design is distinctive: it's a three-arched bridge supporting a parade of shops supporting another bridge. It dates to

candidates.name: Santa Croce
candidates.content: Contains the monumental tombs of Galileo, Michelangelo, Machiavelli, Dante, Rossini, and many other notables in addition to artistic decorations. There is also great artwork in the church. The Museo dell'Opera di Santa Croce (incl

candidates.name: Santa Maria Novella
candidates.content: A beautiful church with great artwork, including a Trinity by Masaccio that is being restored as of April 2024 but can still be seen from the scaffold for an additional charge of €1.50 and a great series of frescoes by Ghirlandaio

candidates.name: Great Synagogue and Jewish Museum of Florence
candidates.price: €6.50 total for the synagogue and museum
candidates.hours: Jun-Sep: Mon-Thu 10:00 - 18:30, Fri 10:00 - 17:00; Oct-May: Sun-Thu 10:00 - 17:30, Fri 10:00 - 15:00. Closed except for religious services on Saturdays and Jewish holidays
candidates.content: Lovely Moorish-style synagogue built in 1882 and a museum with many artefacts and documentation of Florentine Jewish life going back many centuries; audio tours in multiple languages are available.

candidates.name: Boboli Gardens
candidates.content: Elaborately landscaped and with many interesting sculptures, behind the Pitti Palace. Wonderful city views. Don't miss the Bardini gardens. Entrance to that is included in the combination ticket price for the Boboli, and it's a sh

candidates.name: Santa Maria del Fiore
candidates.content: The cathedral interior is to a basilica pattern; it's vast and at first feels dark and empty. Give your eyes time to adjust, and admire the stained glass windows, funeral monument of Bishop d'Orso, and altar of St Zanobius. Below

candidates.name: Palazzo Davanzati
candidates.content: a house museum with antique fittings and furniture

candidates.name: Museo Horne
candidates.content: Displays art and furnishings of the 14th & 15th century. The building and art collection were owned by art historian Herbert Percy Horne.

candidates.name: Archaeological Museum
candidates.content: The Etruscan art collection is particularly good.

candidates.name: Museo Novecento
candidates.hours: Sat-Wed 11:00-20:00, Thu 11:00-14:00, Fri 11:00-23:00, Firenze Cardholder free
candidates.content: Gallery of 20th- & 21st-century art, on three floors of a palazzo.

candidates.name: Stibbert Museum
candidates.content: Has a great collection of armour and arms.

candidates.name: San Lorenzo
candidates.content: The façade of this church was never completed, giving it a striking, rustic appearance. Inside the church is pure Renaissance neo-classical splendor. If you go around the back of the church, there is a separate entrance to the Med

candidates.name: The English Cemetery
candidates.content: In the 19th century, the "English Cemetery" received anyone that the city's churchyards wouldn't receive, e.g. Orthodox Christians, but Britons and Americans were the majority. Famous names here include Elizabeth Barrett Browning,

candidates.name: Piazza della Signoria
candidates.content: Piazza della Signoria is the grand open space in front: not quite a square, as Palazzo Vecchio blocks out one corner. Sights here are the equestrian statue of Cosimo de Medici, the Fountain of Neptune, the statue of David, and Log

candidates.name: Santa Felicita
candidates.content: Contains frescoes of the Annunciation and a painting of the Deposition of Christ by the brilliant and weird mannerist painter, Pontormo. They are to be found in the Barbadori Chapel, which is to your immediate right when entering

candidates.name: San Miniato al Monte
candidates.content: The Sacristy contains frescoes by Spinello Aretino. In the cemetery near this church there are graves of famous people of Florence, including Carlo Lorenzi (Collodi) - author of the famous Pinocchio. Also, turn around when you rea

candidates.name: Baptistery
candidates.content: Octagonal plan, with a pyramidal roof covering its dome. It's famous for its bronze doors by Andrea Pisano (14th century) and Lorenzo Ghiberti (15th century) and a beautiful interior vault decorated with 13th-century mosaics. The

candidates.name: Museo Marini
candidates.content: Houses the work of that contemporary sculptor.

candidates.name: Orsanmichele
candidates.content: A beautiful old church from the 14th century, which once functioned as a grain market.

candidates.name: San Marco Convent
candidates.content: Houses frescoes by Fra Angelico and his workshop. Fra Angelico painted a series of frescoes for the cells in which the Dominican monks lived.

candidates.name: Giotto's Tower
candidates.content: Almost tall, with 414 steps to climb, this richly decorated tower is topped by an open terrace with a panorama of the Duomo, city and surrounds.

candidates.name: Firenze Rafting
candidates.content: Guided rafting trips on the Arno through the historic centre, passing beneath Ponte Vecchio. Tours last about one hour, require no previous experience and are run in inflatable rafts with an instructor in each boat. Equipment is p

candidates.name: Enjoy the view from the Piazzale Michelangelo
candidates.content: It's a big square on a hill, but somewhat distant from the traditional tourist sites. It's easy to reach it even on foot using the stairs called "Rampe di San Niccolò". They are on the side of the Arno RIver just in front of the n

candidates.name: Florence Photography Workshop & Tour
candidates.content: Discover Florence with your camera and with a professional photography teacher (a Vogue-featured American photographer) and an official Florence guide at your side.

candidates.name: Centro Machiavelli
candidates.content: Italian language and cultural school for foreigners. The structure and the contents of the programmes for the levels are based on the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages. The school also organises a programme of c

candidates.name: Michelangelo Institute
candidates.content: Italian study programmes for foreign students. Cooking workshop, art history classes, plastic arts and visual arts programs are also taught in this academy.

candidates.name: Cooking Class
candidates.content: Florence and Tuscany are becoming synonymous with "cooking class". Tuscan cuisine is appreciated worldwide and a cooking class experience is now more and more part of the attraction of Tuscany, as a way of carrying back home memor

candidates.name: Impruneta spa
candidates.content: The thermal waters of Impruneta spring from two sources and are used to treat respiratory diseases, liver, gastrointestinal, and skin allergies.

candidates.name: Scuola Leonardo da Vinci Florence
candidates.content: Offers a wide choice of Italian language and culture courses for children and adults from beginning to advanced levels.

candidates.name: ABC School
candidates.content: Italian language school offering language and cultural courses since 1982.

candidates.name: Istituto Galilei
candidates.content: Italian language school specializing in one-to-one, personalized and small group (max 4 people) full immersion courses.

candidates.name: Cavalli Club
candidates.content: Roberto Cavalli, Italian fashion designer, has one his beautiful clubs in Florence. The inside has a stage with a projector of Roberto Cavalli's fashion shows running non-stop. The upstairs can be a private lounge for parties or V

candidates.name: Bamboo Lounge Club
candidates.content: Bamboo Lounge Club is a great place for young adults and students to party. The music is great from European to American techno and many other worldwide DJs. Bamboo Lounge Club offers VIP tables and has two midsized bars. It is ve

candidates.name: Été
candidates.content: A lovely little café with warm service and good local beer and wine.

candidates.name: Tenax
candidates.content: If you love house and electronic music this is the best club to go to. It’s a two-story club, located on the outskirts of Florence, features DJ’s from all around Europe, America, and Australia. This club also holds many concerts d

candidates.name: La Cite
candidates.content: A very nice and cozy cafe/bookstore. Good prices, nice atmosphere, good books. Borgo San Frediano 20r.

candidates.name: Enoteca Le volpi e l'Uva
candidates.content: The must of the tasting wines and savory titbits. Piazza dei Rossi, 1.

candidates.name: Trattoria Le Mossacce
candidates.content: Reliable local eatery. Local produce and meats are prepared simply using traditional recipes and time-honoured tradition. Some pastas are made fresh daily, so ask for the daily special. If you want to experience Bistecca alla Fior

candidates.name: Enoteca Pinchiorri
candidates.content: Michelin-starred restaurant with exquisite meals at splurge prices.

candidates.name: I fratellini
candidates.content: Good street food: panini for €5 (Mar 2024) and wine for €2+ (Oct 2018) from a tiny hole in the wall. Patrons eat on the sidewalk while resting their glass of wine on small shelves nested along the street wall.

candidates.name: Il Vegetariano
candidates.content: Budget restaurant with more formal front room, the eclectic middle room, or the peaceful outdoor garden in the back. Daily changing menu with vegan and gluten-free items clearly marked, desserts, salads, soups, hearty brown bread,

candidates.name: al Tranvai
candidates.content: Tourists seldom venture this far south. Traditional Tuscan food at decent prices. 1st courses at €7, mains at €10 to €16 and vino at €4 / 0.5L (Oct 2018). The rabbit, asparagus souffle and fiori fritti are excellent and the servic

candidates.name: Trattoria Palle D'Oro dal 1860
candidates.content: Long-standing family-run Tuscan restaurant. This is where the locals come, not least for the low prices. Fixed price 2-course lunch or €13, dinner €14 (Oct 2018)

candidates.name: Pescheria Sugarello
candidates.content: Seafood. Excellent fried calamari and grilled fish fillet with vegetables. You can find also fresh oysters. Be there early, as it gets packed very easily.

candidates.name: Trattoria Zà Zà
candidates.content: A very nicely decorated restaurant with many vegetarian choices. You can choose to sit inside or outside in the piazza. The menu is huge, lots of choices, and the prices are fair. Service is outstanding, they really cater to your

candidates.name: Trattoria da Tito
candidates.content: Although a bit of a walk from the main attractions, this restaurant speaks for itself with mandatory reservations. Great Italian food and atmosphere. Dinner often includes impromptu free drinks and lively table staff.

candidates.name: Self-Service Ristorante Leonardo
candidates.price: Primi €3.5-4. Secondi €4.5-5.5. About €10 per person for a full-course dinner (Oct 2018)
candidates.content: Although there is a menu at the entrance, it is better to go straight in and pick what you like. You can also order Bistecca alla Fiorentina.

candidates.name: Tiona Asian Restaurant
candidates.content: Not that you'd admit to wanting a break from Italian food, but this small friendly Sri Lankan restaurant makes a refreshing change. Ayubowan!

candidates.name: "Il Latini" Restaurant
candidates.content: Fun place, communal seating and lively staff. The steaks are good.
